methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study one accurate model, explain the rule in your own words, repair any gap, and explain it again without copying.
methodBriefing.why: Saying the relationship out loud helps expose missing steps and makes the rule easier to use later.
how: Explain the rule from memory in plain language.
Compare your explanation with the model and fix any missing step.
Explain it again with the correction included.
methodBriefing.completion: You can state the rule accurately, give the key relationship, and correct a common mistake.
personalization: Start with the big picture before details.
Use one step at a time.
Return to retrieval after support fades.

activities.label: Product rule model
activities.title: Product rule structure
activities.body: Study the rule map, then get ready to explain it back in your own words.

essentialIdeas: Differentiate a product by using the product rule on the two function factors.

activities.label: Explain product rule
activities.title: State the product rule
activities.body: Write the rule in your own words. Then compare it with the model.
activities.correctAnswer: When differentiating a product of two functions, take the derivative of the first times the second, plus the first times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and shows that both factors stay involved. If you left out one term, repair by naming the two parts separately.

activities.label: Repair product rule
activities.title: Fix the product step
activities.body: Correct the missing step, then restate the rule once more.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Differentiating a product means differentiating each factor separately and adding the results.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate one factor, keep the other factor unchanged, then add the second factor differentiated with the first unchanged.
activities.feedback: The error is treating the two factors as if they were independent sums. The correct rule keeps both original factors in both terms.

activities.label: Chain rule model
activities.title: Chain rule structure
activities.body: Study the rule map, then get ready to explain it back in your own words.

essentialIdeas: Differentiate a composite function by applying the chain rule to the outer and inner parts.

activities.label: Reexplain chain rule
activities.title: Say the chain rule again
activities.body: Explain the chain rule from memory in plain language.
activities.correctAnswer: For a composite function, differentiate the outer function and multiply by the derivative of the inner function.
activities.feedback: A complete answer shows the outside function first and the inside derivative second. If you said only the outside part, add the inner rate as the multiplier.

activities.label: Rule recognition check
activities.title: Choose the matching rule
activities.body: Pick the rule that fits a function made by putting one function inside another.
choices: Apply the chain rule to the outer and inner functions.
Differentiate each piece separately and add the results.
Use the product rule on the two factors.
Subtract the derivative of the inside from the outside derivative.
activities.correctAnswer: Apply the chain rule to the outer and inner functions.
activities.feedback: A composite function needs the outer derivative times the inner derivative. The other choices describe different rules or an incorrect operation.

targetAssignments.essentialIdea: Differentiate a product by using the product rule on the two function factors.
Differentiate a composite function by applying the chain rule to the outer and inner parts.

items.essentialIdea: Product rule differentiates a product as first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first.

check.title: Differentiate a product
check.prompt: How do you differentiate the product of two functions f and g?
check.referenceAnswer: Differentiate fg as f g' + g f'.
check.feedback: The derivative splits into two terms, one for each factor.

items.essentialIdea: Chain rule differentiates a composite by multiplying the outer derivative by the inner derivative.

check.title: Differentiate a composite
check.prompt: How do you differentiate a composite function like f(g(x))?
check.referenceAnswer: Differentiate the outer function at the inner function, then multiply by g'(x).
check.feedback: The outer derivative is evaluated first, then multiplied by the inner derivative.

recognitionCheck.title: Pick the chain rule
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which derivative rule applies to f(g(x))?
choices: Differentiate the outer function at the inner function, then multiply by the inner derivative.
Differentiate each factor and add the results.
Differentiate only the inner function and ignore the outer function.
Multiply the function by its derivative.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: Differentiate the outer function at the inner function, then multiply by the inner derivative.
recognitionCheck.feedback: That is the chain rule because it links outer and inner derivatives.

idea: Pick the chain rule Which derivative rule applies to f(g(x))? Differentiate the outer function at the inner function, then multiply by the inner derivative. Differentiate each factor and add the results. Differentiate only the inner function and ignore the outer function. Multiply the function by its derivative. That is the chain rule because it links outer and inner derivatives.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study one accurate model exchange, explain the pattern in your own words, repair any gap, and explain it again without copying.
methodBriefing.why: It helps you turn a fixed dialogue into a usable speaking pattern.
how: Close it and explain the question and answer pattern in your own words.
Compare your version with the model and fix any missing part.
Explain the pattern again using a new routine question and answer.
methodBriefing.completion: You can produce the question and a complete present-tense answer without the frame.
personalization: Start from a concrete speaking prompt.
Keep the grammar note tied to speaking.

activities.label: Model the routine exchange
activities.title: Routine question and answer
activities.body: Read the model exchange and notice the question pattern. Then name the two parts you would reuse in speech.

essentialIdeas: Ask when a person does a daily routine with cuándo plus a present-tense verb.
Answer with a complete present-tense sentence that names the routine and the time.

activities.label: Explain the pattern
activities.title: Say the pattern in your words
activities.body: In Spanish, explain how you ask when someone does a routine and how you answer. Keep it short.
activities.concept: Ask when a person does a daily routine with cuándo plus a present-tense verb.
activities.correctAnswer: You ask with cuándo plus the present-tense verb, and you answer with a complete present-tense sentence that names the routine and the time.
activities.feedback: A complete answer states both parts of the exchange: the question form and the full present-tense reply. If it only names vocabulary, it needs the sentence pattern.

activities.label: Repair the sentence frame
activities.title: Fix the answer frame
activities.body: Your reply is missing one needed part. Correct it so it is a complete present-tense sentence.
activities.misconceptionSummary: The learner may give only a verb or time expression instead of a complete present-tense sentence.
activities.concept: Answer with a complete present-tense sentence that names the routine and the time.
activities.correctAnswer: Yo me ducho a las siete.
activities.feedback: The repair must include a full subject-verb sentence, not just a verb or a time. A complete reply tells what routine happens and when it happens.

activities.label: Explain it again
activities.title: Use a new routine question
activities.body: Say the pattern again with a different routine. Do not copy the model sentence.
activities.concept: Ask when a person does a daily routine with cuándo plus a present-tense verb.
activities.feedback: This check shows whether you can reuse the question pattern without the frame. The question should still ask when the routine happens and use the present tense.

activities.label: Choose the correct exchange
activities.title: Pick the best exchange
activities.body: Choose the response that best fits a question about a daily routine.
activities.concept: Answer with a complete present-tense sentence that names the routine and the time.
choices: Yo me baño a las ocho.
activities.correctAnswer: Yo me baño a las ocho.
activities.feedback: The correct choice is a full present-tense sentence with the routine and the time. The other options leave out the sentence frame or form it incorrectly.

items.essentialIdea: Daily routine questions about completion use when plus a complete present-tense sentence.

check.title: Answer a routine time question
check.prompt: How do you ask when someone completes a daily activity, and how do you answer it in one complete present-tense sentence?
check.referenceAnswer: Ask with when, then answer with a complete present-tense sentence such as She finishes breakfast at 7:00.
check.feedback: Use when for completion time and answer with a full present-tense sentence.

items.essentialIdea: Daily routine completion answers stay in present tense and give the time clearly.

check.title: State routine completion time
check.prompt: How do you respond to a question about when someone completes a daily activity?
check.referenceAnswer: Respond with a complete present-tense sentence that gives the time, such as He leaves for school at 8:00.
check.feedback: Keep the sentence in present tense and include the completion time.

recognitionCheck.title: Choose the correct routine reply
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which response best answers when someone completes a daily activity?
recognitionCheck.feedback: The correct choice is present tense and gives the time in a complete sentence.
